summary.business: GE Power India Limited provides a comprehensive portfolio of power generation products and services, including boilers, environmental solutions like Flue Gas Desulphurization (FGD) and De-NOx systems, and a full suite of services for thermal power plants. The company serves major domestic power generation entities such as NTPC and Adani, focusing on core services, equipment upgrades, and selective equipment supply rather than full EPC contracts. Its operations are supported by an execution center in Noida and a robust global supply chain network.

Services: Emergency generator repair (shop floor and on-site)
Boilers: Mill door seal collar assembly and dipper flange revamping

currentContext.strengths: Deep integration within India's power infrastructure sector with long-standing relationships with key entities like NTPC.|Unique capabilities in emergency generator repair, reducing generation loss and improving grid availability.|Strategic focus on high-margin, cash-accretive services and asset-light models, enhancing operational resilience.|Strong operational excellence culture (Lean, GE Vernova Way) driving differentiation and cost optimization.
currentContext.strategies: Renewable energy capacity has crossed 250 GW and now accounts for nearly half of India's total installed capacity of around 520 GW, with a target of achieving 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity, reinforcing a diversified and resilient energy mix.|The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change's revision of flue gas desulphurization installation norms for thermal power stations has provided greater regulatory clarity while enabling continued reliable baseload supply alongside progressive emission reduction.
currentContext.expansion: The Company is focused on continued growth in its core services segment, selective participation in equipment upgrade opportunities from India's large thermal renovation pipeline, and a measured approach to FGD equipment supply (EP) rather than full EPC undertakings. The execution center in Noida, along with a robust supply chain network across India and globally, underpins the Company's operational capabilities.

risks.risk: Evolving trade policies and tariff escalations
risks.note: Introduced near-term volatility and tested adaptability of businesses and supply chains worldwide, requiring diversified sourcing strategies to maintain operational stability.
Revision of flue gas desulphurization installation norms for thermal power stations provides clarity but also imposes compliance requirements that could affect operations and costs.
While coal continues to play a role in India's energy mix, the strategic balancing towards renewable energy may reduce long-term demand for thermal power equipment and services.

risks.risk: Execution risk in selective project participation
risks.note: Measured approach to FGD equipment supply (EP) rather than full EPC undertakings limits exposure but also caps revenue potential from large turnkey projects.
Global developments underscored the critical role of diversified sourcing strategies; reliance on a robust supply chain network across India and globally exposes the company to potential disruptions.

one-line thesis: GE Power India is executing a hard turnaround into an **asset-light thermal-power services** company, and is now carving out its last heavy-manufacturing drag. Two years of "value over volume" took **net worth ₹57cr → ₹483cr** (>8x), **EBITDA −₹251cr (FY23) → +₹277cr (FY26)**, **cash −₹66cr (2023) → ₹880cr (Mar-26)** (18x), shed **₹1,364cr of bank-guarantee exposure**, lifted the ICRA rating to **BBB+ stable**, and restored a dividend. The capstone: **demerging the loss-making Durgapur boiler/pressure-vessel plant to JSW Energy** (139 GEPIL : 10 JSW Energy shares, no GEPIL dilution) to remove a ~₹27cr/yr average loss and sharpen the pure-services focus.
financial scorecard (multi-year turnarou:
| Metric | Latest | Prior / start | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Net worth | **₹483cr** (Mar-26) | ₹57cr (Mar-24) | >8-fold in 2 years; "deliberate cash-accretive strategy" |
| Cash / liquidity | **₹880cr** (Mar-26) | −₹66cr deficit (2023) | ~18-fold improvement |
| EBITDA | **+₹277cr** (FY26) | −₹251cr loss (FY23) | swung from loss to positive |
| Bank-guarantee exposure | shed **₹1,364cr** over 2 yrs | — | "untethering capital from historical burdens" |
| Credit rating | **BBB+ / stable** (ICRA, Jun-26) | (upgraded) | long-term rating |
| Order bookings (total) | **₹734cr** (FY26) | ₹299cr (FY22) | ~25% CAGR; FY26 **+34%** in core services |
| oOEM (other-OEM) order intake | **~₹320cr** | ₹162cr | third-party fleet segment ("very unique for your company") |
| Dividend | declared in **2026** | — | first in the recovery |
> One-offs / structural: **Hydro and Gas slump sale** and the **BHEL settlement** are already-completed portfolio actions cited as part of the two-year cleanup. Durgapur booked an **average ~₹27cr/yr loss (2023–2025)** — the drag the demerger removes. Retrospective demerger effective date **1-Jul-2025**.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue / margin:** no explicit forward numeric guidance given; strategy is "value over volume" — high-margin, cash-accretive, faster-cash-conversion services.
- **Order inflow:** core-services order bookings have compounded ~25% (₹299cr→₹734cr); FY26 +34% in core services — management frames services as the growth engine, but gave **no FY27 inflow target number**.
- **Supply-chain independence:** post-demerger, **"full supply chain independence targeted to be achieved very soon"** (concurrent with a 5-yr JSW Energy manufacturing services agreement as bridge).
- **Demerger timeline:** transitions on NCLT sanction, retrospectively effective **1-Jul-2025**; shareholder vote invited.
- **Capex / commissioning dates:** none — this is a divestiture, not an expansion call.
order book & pipeline:
- Total order bookings **₹299cr (FY22) → ₹734cr (FY26)**, ~25% CAGR; **+34% growth in core services in FY26**.
- **oOEM (third-party / other-OEM fleet) segment**: order intake grew **₹162cr → ~₹320cr** — management highlights this as a differentiated, service-led lever ("very unique for your company").
- International reach expanded: **Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Austria, UAE, Malaysia, Indonesia, Morocco**.
segment / subsidiary detail — the durgap:
- **What Durgapur is:** West Bengal facility making **power boiler components, pressure vessels, pipings, coal mills** for thermal plants; **~661 acres leasehold** (industrial factory unit + residential township).
- **Why exit:** utilization fell to mostly service/non-coal work; **significant underutilization 2023–2025** → **~₹27cr/yr average loss** booked in GEPIL. Management evaluated retention vs demerger and chose demerger to simplify the portfolio.
- **Acquirer:** **JSW Energy Ltd** (listed IPP) — expected to improve facility utilization given the broader Indian power-demand outlook.
- **Structure:** Scheme of Arrangement; going-concern, as-is-where-is; **retrospectively effective 1-Jul-2025** on NCLT sanction.
- **Entitlement:** **139 GEPIL shares → 10 JSW Energy shares** (third-party independent valuers + formal Fairness Opinion). **GEPIL shareholding unchanged / no dilution** — shareholders keep full GEPIL stake AND get direct JSW Energy shares.
- **Continuity safeguard:** **5-year manufacturing services agreement with JSW Energy** reserves capacity at pre-agreed schedules/pricing so core-services execution isn't disrupted; independent supply chain being built in parallel ("full independence very soon").
- **Governance:** Board unanimously approved; shareholders invited to vote.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Services-led model** (core services + oOEM third-party fleet) as the go-forward engine; portfolio simplification frees focus/capital for it.
- International-market expansion (7 named geographies) as a services growth vector.
- Post-demerger **pure-play services entity** with a clean balance sheet (net worth ₹483cr, cash ₹880cr) and restored rating/dividend — optionality to redeploy capital.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Strategic pivot: **"stopped chasing volume for the sake of revenue; began chasing value for the sake of profitability"** — favouring high-margin, cash-accretive work with faster cash-conversion cycles.
- Removing Durgapur's ~₹27cr/yr average loss is directly margin-accretive to the continuing entity.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): - **No expansion capex announced** — the call is about divesting an underutilized asset, not building. The only "watch" items are corporate-action milestones: NCLT sanction of the scheme and achievement of independent supply chain.
capital allocation:
- Deleveraging-first: shed **₹1,364cr** bank-guarantee exposure; reduced outstanding bond exposure; rebuilt cash to **₹880cr**.
- **Dividend restored in 2026** as a signal of restored financial strength.
- Demerger is structured as **no-dilution** for GEPIL holders (they receive JSW Energy shares on top of unchanged GEPIL holding).
risks & watch-items:
- **Execution / continuity risk** of separating manufacturing: relies on a 5-yr JSW Energy services agreement + building an independent supply chain "very soon" — slippage would pressure core-services delivery.
- **NCLT-sanction / shareholder-vote risk** — the scheme is proposed, not yet sanctioned; retrospective 1-Jul-2025 effective date.
- **No fresh quarterly P&L disclosed** — turnaround metrics are multi-year; investors can't see current-quarter run-rate here.
- Structural dependence on the **thermal-power aftermarket** cycle and on the **GE Vernova / JSW ecosystem** for manufacturing support.
management quality / tone: - Confident, disciplined-turnaround narrative; candid about Durgapur's underutilization and losses. Emphasis on "value over volume", cash conversion, and no-dilution shareholder alignment. Fully scripted management presentation — **no analyst Q&A to stress-test claims**, so credibility is best judged against the multi-year balance-sheet figures they disclosed.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The **buyer is JSW Energy** — a thermal/RE IPP that already backward-integrates equipment (per companies.csv it holds the GE Power boiler business / Toshiba-JSW TG JV); the 661-acre boiler/pressure-vessel plant plus a 5-yr reserved-capacity agreement deepens JSW's in-house thermal-equipment capability.
- **GEPIL becomes a near-pure asset-light services entity** with a clean balance sheet (cash ₹880cr, net worth ₹483cr) — the demerger is the last big step of the two-year cleanup (after Hydro/Gas slump sale + BHEL settlement).
- The **oOEM (third-party fleet) segment doubling** (₹162cr→₹320cr) is the quiet structural story — servicing non-GE thermal fleets widens the addressable base beyond the captive installed base.
